content.title: About
content.content: Red pickled cabbage is a fermented product made from fresh red (purple) cabbage heads that undergo a brining process with salt, vinegar, sugar and spices. Fermentation preserves vitamins and gives it a characteristic tangy‑sweet flavor, making it a popular side dish and ingredient in salads, sandwiches and Asian‑style meals.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Red cabbage is rich in anthocyanins, pigments that give it a vivid color and act as antioxidants.
Pickling cabbage dates back to ancient Slavic and Germanic cuisines, where fermentation was a key method for long‑term vegetable storage.
During fermentation, probiotic bacteria of the Lactobacillus genus develop, supporting gut health.
Pickled red cabbage is often served as a garnish for meat, fish dishes and layered salads such as the Russian "herring under a fur coat".
In Japan a similar fermented cabbage called "tsukuna" is usually made from white cabbage; the red version is less common but gaining popularity.

items.title: High in vitamin C
items.content: Red cabbage provides over 100 mg of vitamin C per 100 g, supporting immune function and collagen synthesis.

items.title: Antioxidants
items.content: Anthocyanins and polyphenols protect cells from oxidative stress and may reduce the risk of chronic diseases.

items.title: Probiotics
items.content: Fermentation creates live bacteria that promote a healthy intestinal microbiome and improve digestion.

items.title: Dietary fiber
items.content: The cabbage is a good source of fiber, helping regulate blood sugar and increase satiety.

items.title: Minerals
items.content: It contains potassium, calcium and iron, important for heart, bone and blood health.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: Pickled cabbage contains a notable amount of salt; people with hypertension should limit intake.

items.title: Cabbage allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to cabbage or fermentation by‑products.

items.title: Digestive discomfort
items.content: Large portions can cause gas and bloating in those with sensitive stomachs.

items.title: Quality control
items.content: Improperly fermented cabbage may harbor harmful bacteria; purchase from reputable producers.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Eat it straight as a snack, add to salads, sandwiches, tacos, wraps and soups. It pairs well with carrots, apples, nuts and spices such as cumin or coriander. Before serving, you can gently squeeze out excess brine.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep pickled cabbage refrigerated at 0‑4 °C in a sealed container. Shelf life is typically 3‑6 months. Discard if you notice off‑odors, mold or discoloration.
